target: APG initial focus changes with dialog content, scrolling and consequence
observed_behavior: The APG modal pattern describes first-focusable placement as common rather than absolute. When a dialog begins with meaningful lists, tables or multiple paragraphs, it advises focusing an initially non-tabbable static element with tabindex=-1 so users can navigate the structures, and omitting a combined aria-describedby announcement in that situation. When the first interactive element would scroll the start of lengthy content out of view, it advises initially focusing a static top element. For a hard-to-reverse final step such as deleting data or completing a financial transaction, it advises considering the least destructive action. For simple informational/continue dialogs, it advises considering the most frequently used action.
context: W07 B3 K3 read-only APG Keyboard Interaction — Note 1; first-party non-normative explanatory guidance, bounded to qualified APG pattern and exceptions.
limitations: Alternative focus locations are explicitly conditional on semantic content, scrolling, reversibility and likely task usage; no universal first-input, first-button or destructive-action focus rule follows.
The discussion is explanatory recommendation for APG's modal pattern, not normative browser focus algorithm evidence.
Static initial focus with tabindex=-1 is not equivalent to declaring that every dialog control has a nonnegative tabindex.
No assistive-technology reading, scroll behavior or destructive workflow was executed.
